title: Regional dedicated: soft-reserve orchestration, autoscale grace windows, and residency enforcement playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Author a runbook and implementation plan for a regional/multi-zone dedicated fleet strategy that guarantees throughput SLAs using soft-reserve capacity, defines safe autoscale down/up grace windows, and enforces data residency constraints during placement and failover. This ticket covers policy design, runtime hooks, rollout plan, observability, and operational playbook for incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc approved by infra and product
Prototype autoscaler implements soft-reserve and grace windows in staging
Placement decisions annotated with residency tags and validated by e2e tests
Failover playbook documented with steps for automatic and manual interventions
Dashboards show correct metrics (reserved_capacity, spillover_rate, residency_violations) and alerts for SLA violations

design_decisions: Use soft-reserve (percentage of pool) instead of hard partitioning to maximize utilization while guaranteeing tail capacity
Autoscaler behavior: fast scale-up (60s cooldown) + conservative scale-down (300s grace) when soft-reserve is active to preserve KV cache and reduce churn
Spillover policy: prefer same-region zone, then region-peering lane; respect per-customer residency flags that can disable cross-region spillover
Telemetry: add reserved_capacity, available_reserved, spillover_rate, residency_violation_count, prewarm_latency_ms metrics
Cost accounting: label spillover allocations with cost_center and spillover_cost boolean for billing reconciliation
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Cross-zone spillover may breach data residency for regulated customers. Mitigation: residency flag at allocation time; enforcement prevents cross-zone placement and triggers capacity alerts.
Risk: Aggressive scale-down causes cold KV cache misses and latency spikes. Mitigation: implement scale-down grace windows and delta-based node removal (drain smallest-impact slices first).

Risk: Soft-reserve reduces peak utilization and increases unit cost. Mitigation: tiered soft-reserve by contract (committed customers get higher reserve), autoscaler uses predictive prewarm to reduce cost impact.
